# Site images: where they go, the rules, and the generation prompts

Agent websites (WEB_RENDERER.md) used to have just one image, the agent's photo. To look finished on day one (DECISIONS #78) and to sell in the "Best offers" family (DECISIONS #76), a site needs a small set of **bundled illustrations**, plus the images agents and admins upload. This doc lists every image slot, the rules every image follows, and the generation prompt for each bundled image.

**Status:** designed on 2026-10-18 (DECISIONS #81; desktop LCP refined by #82). **All 20 images were generated by the user on 2026-10-18.** The masters are in `design/site-images/source/<slot>.png`, with the original titles in `MAPPING.md`. The first `interest-money-back` was rejected (its path markers carried English text and looked like gravestones) and regenerated from the corrected prompt.

**Pending (DECISIONS #93, 2026-10-22):** five new plan-type images for the interests added with every insurance type, `interest-motor`, `interest-home`, `interest-travel`, `interest-business` and `interest-accident` (prompts below, for the user to generate). Until they exist, the renderer shows the generic `interest-other` illustration on their cards (with `alt=""`), so their cards are never bare; once each master is in `design/site-images/source/` and `scripts/gen-site-images.py` has run, it is used automatically (no catalog or code change).

The renderer only draws a bundled image that is listed in `web/images/manifest.json`, so a missing file just means no image, never a broken one. The 18 are converted and shipped in `web/images/` (see "Generating the WebP files"); the masters stay in `design/` and are never copied to the site.

## Rules for every image
1. **No stock faces pretending to be real people.**
   - The agent is only ever shown in their own uploaded photo.
   - Customers and testimonials never get faces, since an invented face next to a quote is fabricated social proof.
   - The illustrations show generic, clearly illustrated people, never photo-real ones.
2. **No brands.** No insurer logos, product names, building signage, LIC colours or mascots. No text, letters or numbers inside an image, because text is set in HTML so it can be translated and indexed.
3. **One house style:** flat, editorial vector illustration (the style prefix below), so the 5 templates and all agents look like one product.
4. **Brand palette, accent-neutral:** the site is cool, neutral and white (`design-tokens.json`: background `#FFFFFF`, cards `#F9FAFB`, greys `#F3F4F6`–`#6B7280`, ink `#111827`). The agent's accent (one of 8 deep swatches, from indigo to rust) must stay the only strong colour on the page. Images therefore use the brand's cool greys for most shapes, soft ink `#374151` for outlines and hair, and only two pale, low-saturation tints in small areas: dusty blue-grey `#C9D3E3` and pale sage `#CFDCD3`. Skin tones are warm and natural. Never saturated colour, never warm earth tones (terracotta and mustard clash with indigo, teal and slate, and compete with maroon and rust), and no large flat colour blocks (DESIGN_SYSTEM.md).
4a. **Pure white edges:** the background is pure white `#FFFFFF`, and the scene fades softly into it with no frame or tinted box, so the image blends into the white page and the `#F9FAFB` cards.
5. **Indian context:** everyday modern Indian homes and clothing. A mix of ages, regions and genders across the set; no religious symbols; no wealth cliches (no gold, no cash bundles, no luxury cars).
5a. **The agent is the only advisor:** the site's copy is the agent speaking in the first person ("I help families…", "Leave me a message"). An illustrated advisor would look like a second agent, so images show the **customer's side** (families, people at home, people sending a message), never an illustrated insurance agent.
6. **Composition leaves space:** the subject sits in the left or right two-thirds, with calm empty background on the other side. That side is the safe area for responsive crops (`object-position`).
7. **Formats:** generate a PNG master of at least 1600 px on the long side, saved to `design/site-images/source/<name>.png`. `scripts/gen-site-images.py` writes WebP at 400 and 800 px wide (and 1200×630 for the OG images) into `web/images/`, and updates `web/images/manifest.json`. **Budget:** 800 px files ≤ 45 KB, 400 px ≤ 18 KB, OG ≤ 80 KB.
8. **HTML:**
   - every bundled image has explicit `width`/`height`, `srcset` and `sizes`, `decoding="async"` and `loading="lazy"`;
   - the only eager image is the agent's hero photo (the LCP element; WEB_RENDERER.md), and the hero scene on Best offers templates is `fetchpriority="low"`;
   - `alt` is a translated text (`site.image_alt_*`), or `alt=""` when the image is purely decorative.
9. **Licence:** use a generator whose terms allow commercial use. Don't name artists or studios in prompts. Keep the prompt and the tool used next to each master (`design/site-images/source/<name>.txt`).

## Where images go
| # | Slot | Templates | Source | Aspect / size | Why | Fallback |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Hero portrait** | all | **agent upload** (exists) | 1:1, shown up to 240 px | The agent is the product; the speech bubbles reuse it as a 32 px avatar | Initials monogram in CSS, **never** a stock face |
| 2 | **Hero scene** | spotlight, guide | bundled, 3 variants | 4:3, 800 px | Sets an emotional context (family, future) beside the featured offer | No image; the layout closes up |
| 3 | **Plan-type images**, one per `catalog.interests` key (13; 5 pending) | all: Services cards; Best offers: plan cards when there are no offers; any offer without its own image | bundled, `catalog.interests[].image` | 16:9, 400/800 px | Makes services and offers scannable and gives every card a picture from day one | The generic `interest-other` image (`alt=""`) while an interest's own isn't shipped; icon-only if that's missing too |
| 4 | **Offer image** | Offers section cards (never the hero banner) | **admin upload** per offer (designed, OFFERS.md); demo offers bundled for fixtures | 16:9, 800 px | A specific visual for each offer | The plan-type image for the offer's `interest`, then none |
| 5 | **"Let's talk" image** | all: contact section, and the thank-you state | bundled | 4:3, 400/800 px | Carries the conversation theme into the enquiry form | No image |
| 6 | **Share (OG) image** when the agent has no photo | all | bundled, 2 (one per family) | 1200×630 | WhatsApp and social previews always show a picture | `summary` card with no image |
| 7 | Template previews | app picker | screenshots (exists) | 390×844 | Not generated: rendered from fixtures (WEB_RENDERER.md) | n/a |

Not given images, on purpose: about (the agent's photo is enough), highlights (SVG icons), achievements and testimonials (no fabricated faces), FAQ (text reads better), and the unavailable page.

**Which variant:** the hero scene is picked from its 3 variants deterministically from the slug, like the seed copy (DECISIONS #78). An agent can't choose it yet.

## Style prefix (put in front of every prompt)
> Flat editorial vector illustration, soft rounded shapes, gentle soft shadows, clean and minimal. Pure white background (#FFFFFF), the scene fading softly into the white with no frame, border or tinted backdrop, and lots of empty white space. Cool neutral palette: light greys (#F3F4F6, #E5E7EB, #D1D5DB), mid grey (#9CA3AF), soft dark ink (#374151) for outlines and hair, with small touches of pale dusty blue-grey (#C9D3E3) and pale sage (#CFDCD3) only. Warm natural Indian skin tones, modern everyday Indian clothing in the same muted greys and pale tints. Calm, honest, reassuring, no hype. Clean composition for a professional, modern website.

**Negative prompt (every image):**
> text, letters, numbers, words, captions, watermark, signature, logo, brand, signage, currency notes, coins piles, gold jewellery heaps, luxury car, hospital gore, needles close-up, sad or crying faces, religious symbols, flags, photorealistic, 3D render, saturated colours, bright blue, red, orange, terracotta, mustard, yellow, neon, cream or beige background, coloured backdrop, frame, border, harsh contrast, heavy grain, cluttered background, insurance agent, salesperson, suit and tie, distorted hands, extra fingers

## Prompts
Each prompt follows the style prefix. **[safe-left]** means: keep the left third empty (the subject is on the right). **[safe-right]** is the opposite.

### 2. Hero scenes (`hero-scene-1..3`, 4:3)
- **hero-scene-1, a young family at home** [safe-left]: A young Indian couple in their early thirties sits on a sofa in a bright, simple living room, with their daughter of about six leaning on her father's shoulder, all relaxed and smiling. A potted plant and a window with soft morning light. Feels secure and unhurried.
- **hero-scene-2, planning together** [safe-left]: A middle-aged Indian couple at a small dining table looks at a tablet together, the woman pointing at the screen, both calm and confident. A cup of chai, a notebook and a pen on the table; soft evening light from a side lamp. Feels like a good decision being made.
- **hero-scene-3, three generations** [safe-left]: A grandmother in a simple cotton saree, her son and his teenage son walk side by side along a tree-lined neighbourhood lane, mid-conversation and laughing. low-rise homes in the background, leafy green-grey trees. Feels like continuity and care across generations.

### 3. Plan-type images (16:9; names from `catalog.interests[].image`: `interest-<key>`, with `_` written as `-`)
- **interest-term, family protection** [safe-right]: A father kneels to tie his young son's shoelace at the front door while the mother stands behind them holding a school bag; a large, soft abstract leaf shape arches protectively over the family. Morning, everyday, safe.
- **interest-endowment, steady savings** [safe-right]: A young woman waters a small plant on a balcony; beside it, three simple grey pots hold plants of increasing size, in a row. Calm, patient growth.
- **interest-money-back, money at milestones** [safe-right]: A young Indian couple walks hand in hand along a winding garden path towards a bench under a tree; along the path, three small flowering shrubs, each in fuller bloom than the last. Suggests rewards along the journey. **No stones, signs, markers or plaques of any kind, and no icons or charts.**
- **interest-child, a child's future** [safe-right]: A girl of about ten in a school uniform reads a big book at a desk by a window, with a small globe and a paper rocket nearby, while her mother watches proudly from the doorway. Curiosity and possibility.
- **interest-pension, retirement income** [safe-right]: A retired Indian couple in their sixties shares tea on a sunny verandah, the husband reading a newspaper and the wife laughing, with potted tulsi and a bicycle leaning on the wall. Independent, content, unhurried.
- **interest-health, health cover** [safe-right]: A friendly woman doctor in a white coat talks with a middle-aged man and his wife in a bright, clean clinic room; the man holds a simple folder. Reassuring, caring, no medical equipment close-up.
- **interest-ulip, market-linked growth** [safe-right]: A young professional woman at a light wooden desk looks at a laptop showing an abstract rising line made of soft rounded shapes (no numbers), with a small sapling in a pot beside the laptop. Smart, forward-looking, not flashy.
- **interest-motor, vehicle cover (pending)** [safe-right]: A young Indian man and his father stand beside a parked small family hatchback and a scooter in a quiet residential lane in the morning, the father handing him the keys with a smile. The vehicles are plain and unbranded, in soft greys, with no number plates, badges or logos. Everyday, safe, unhurried; no damage, accident or road scene.
- **interest-home, home and belongings (pending)** [safe-right]: A middle-aged Indian woman locks the front door of a modest, tidy home with a small potted plant and a doormat, while her husband waters a plant on the step; a soft abstract leaf shape arches gently over the doorway, as in `interest-term`. Calm and secure; no fire, flood or break-in imagery.
- **interest-travel, trips in India or abroad (pending)** [safe-right]: A young Indian couple with a small rolling suitcase and a backpack walks out of their home towards the street, the woman checking a phone (blank screen) and the man smiling, with a few soft cloud shapes and a faint abstract path line curving ahead of them. Light, hopeful; no aeroplane close-up, airport signage, flags or landmarks.
- **interest-business, a shop or small business (pending)** [safe-right]: A shopkeeper in her forties stands behind the counter of a neat small neighbourhood shop with simple shelves of plain, unlabelled boxes and jars, talking with a customer; a calm, organised scene. No brand names, price tags, signboards or cash.
- **interest-accident, personal accident cover (pending)** [safe-right]: An Indian man in his thirties walks on a park path with a light arm sling, smiling and talking with his wife beside him, their young son running ahead; soft morning light and trees. Recovery and support, reassuring; no injury close-up, blood, hospital equipment or ambulance.
- **interest-other, advice for anything** [safe-right]: A young Indian couple sits at their dining table at home with a few papers and a phone, relaxed and smiling as they talk it through, with soft empty speech-bubble shapes floating above them (no text). Questions being answered, calmly.

### 4. Demo offer images (16:9; for fixtures and the preview's demo company only; admins upload real ones)
These match `supabase/demo/demo-offers.json`. The offers' public names are already disguised (DECISIONS #77); these images must not hint at the real product either.
- **offer-pension-locked-rate** [safe-right]: A couple in their late fifties sits on a park bench, the wife resting her hand on her husband's arm, both looking ahead at a soft sun rising over gentle hills. A settled, certain future.
- **offer-family-health-cash** [safe-right]: A mother sits beside her son's bed in a bright, simple hospital room, holding his hand and smiling, with a get-well flower in a glass on the side table. Comfort, not illness.
- **offer-cancer-care** [safe-right]: Two women friends of about forty walk together in a park at sunrise, one with a light headscarf, arm in arm and smiling, with a soft ribbon-like curve in the sky (not a cancer-ribbon symbol). Strength and support, hopeful.
- **offer-savings-booster** [safe-right]: A young woman in her thirties waters a row of potted plants on a sunny windowsill, each pot a little taller than the last, the last one just coming into bloom. Patient saving that pays off later, calm and steady.
- **offer-simple-protection** [safe-right]: A young mother holds her baby close at a window while a gentle umbrella-shaped arch of leaves shelters them from soft rain outside. Simple, warm protection.
- **offer-couples-savings** [safe-right]: A newly married Indian couple plants a sapling together in a small garden, both holding the same watering can. Partnership and shared future.

### 5. "Let's talk" image (`contact-talk`, 4:3)
- **contact-talk** [safe-left]: A young Indian woman sits comfortably on a sofa at home, typing a message on her phone and smiling, while a soft, empty speech bubble floats up from the phone and a second bubble answers it from the left (no text). Reaching out is easy, and someone replies.

### 6. Share (OG) images (1200×630; used only when the agent has no photo)
- **og-personal** [safe-left, keep the left half empty]: The `interest-other` scene, simplified and placed in the right half: the couple at their table, smiling, with one soft empty speech bubble above them.
- **og-offers** [safe-left, keep the left half empty]: A neat fan of three blank, rounded cards with soft leaf, umbrella and sun shapes on them (no text), floating above a small table plant. Suggests choice and good options.

## Asking agents for their photo (slot 1)
The app's photo step (UX.md) should give these tips, since it's the image that matters most:
- face and shoulders, looking at the camera, in daylight facing a window;
- a plain background;
- smart everyday clothes;
- no sunglasses, no group photos;
- no insurer uniform or logos (DECISIONS #77).

The tips are in the app: UX.md, Onboarding step 1.

## Generating the WebP files (`scripts/gen-site-images.py`)
- **Run:** `python3 -I scripts/gen-site-images.py` from the repo root (Pillow 12; optional `--src` and `--out`). It reads only the top-level `design/site-images/source/*.png` (`spare/` and `needs-fix/` are ignored) and rewrites `web/images/`.
- **Output:** for each master `<name>.png`: `<name>-400.webp` and `<name>-800.webp` at the master's own aspect (16:9 masters give 800×450, 4:3 give 800×600); for `og-*` masters a single `og-<name>-1200.webp`, centre-cropped to 1200×630. WebP files whose master is gone are deleted, so the folder always equals the manifest (a test checks this, and that no PNG is in `web/images/`).
- **Budgets:** each file starts at quality 82; a file over its budget is re-encoded 4 points lower (with a warning) until it fits, and the script fails below quality 40.
- **Manifest:** `web/images/manifest.json` = `{ "<name>": { "w": 800, "h": 450, "sizes": [400, 800] } }` (OG: `{ "w": 1200, "h": 630, "sizes": [1200] }`); `w`/`h` are the largest file's pixels. The renderer draws an image only when its name is listed (WEB_RENDERER.md, "Bundled images"), with `src` = the largest size and `srcset` = every size.
- **Demo offer images** are used only by the dev fixtures: a fixture offer names one in its optional `image` field (copied from `supabase/demo/demo-offers.json`), and the renderer accepts it only when it matches `^offer-[a-z0-9-]+$` and is in the manifest. Real offers use the admin-uploaded `image_url`, else the interest image.
- **Shipped (2026-10-18), all at quality 82, 640 KB in total:** 400 px files 5.7–12.0 KB, 800 px files 15.3–33.1 KB (largest: `hero-scene-3-800` 33.1 KB), `og-personal-1200` 30.6 KB, `og-offers-1200` 13.7 KB.
